s1.syndrome_frame: subacute pulmonary syndrome with hemoptysis and systemic inflammation
key_facts: 10-day history of hemoptysis
1-month history of mild cough, sputum production, and rhinorrhea
elevated C-reactive protein level of 7 mg/dL
normal white-cell count with a neutrophil count of 3.97 × 10^3/μL
negative HIV testing
negative initial microbiologic studies
chest radiograph showed multiple nodules and masses in both lung fields
cavitary lesions had thick, irregular walls with septa-like structures
bronchoscopy revealed diffuse granulomatous inflammation
histopathologic analysis showed diffuse necrotizing granulomatous inflammation
methenamine silver staining revealed yeast-like structures with septate hyphae

shortlist.label: invasive aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: histopathologic analysis showed diffuse necrotizing granulomatous inflammation and methenamine silver staining revealed yeast-like structures with septate hyphae, consistent with aspergillosis

shortlist.label: histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: clinical presentation of subacute pulmonary syndrome with hemoptysis and systemic inflammation, and histopathologic analysis showed diffuse necrotizing granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: clinical presentation of subacute pulmonary syndrome with hemoptysis and systemic inflammation, and histopathologic analysis showed diffuse necrotizing granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: clinical presentation of subacute pulmonary syndrome with hemoptysis and systemic inflammation, and histopathologic analysis showed diffuse necrotizing granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: chronic pulmonary aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: clinical presentation of subacute pulmonary syndrome with hemoptysis and systemic inflammation, and histopathologic analysis showed diffuse necrotizing granulomatous inflammation and methenamine silver staining revealed yeast-like structures with septate hyphae

raw.rationale: The presence of diffuse necrotizing granulomatous inflammation, yeast-like structures with septate hyphae demonstrating acute-angle branching on methenamine silver staining, and the 'halo sign' on chest CT are characteristic findings of invasive aspergillosis.

rejected.label: histoplasmosis
rejected.why: Lack of specific findings such as bird or bat exposure history and the presence of yeast forms in tissues without the characteristic morphology of Histoplasma capsulatum

rejected.label: blastomycosis
rejected.why: The absence of broad-based budding yeast forms in tissues, which are typical for Blastomyces dermatitidis

rejected.label: cryptococcosis
rejected.why: The absence of Cryptococcus neoformans in cerebrospinal fluid or tissues, and the lack of characteristic mucoid capsule on histopathology

rejected.label: chronic pulmonary aspergillosis
rejected.why: The acute presentation and the presence of diffuse necrotizing granulomatous inflammation are more suggestive of an invasive rather than chronic process
